Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath starting about 1 hour ago while resting; accompanied by a cough that began yesterday.
- History of presenting illness: SOB began suddenly over the last hour; no chest pain reported; deep breaths cause chest tenderness; heart rate sensation described as faster than usual.
- Relevant events: Recent cesarean delivery 4 weeks ago.
- Respiratory/constitutional symptoms: Cough started yesterday; no productive cough reported; no fever noted.
- Cardiac symptoms: Heartfelt sensation of increased rate; no chest pain at rest.
- Past medical history: Not otherwise documented in the visit notes.
- Medications: Codeine used after the cesarean section; reported as used regularly but likely not currently daily (last week-ish). Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (allergic reaction not specified).
- Social history: Present with baby; partner at work; no one else with patient at home.
- Surgical history: Cesarean delivery 4 weeks ago.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- General/appearance: Not described.
- Cardiac: Patient self-reported heartbeat felt fast; counted 30 heartbeats during a counting exercise performed on the phone.
- Respiratory: Shortness of breath reported; chest sore on deep inspiration; no chest pain reported.
- Chest/abdomen: C-section scar described as tender.
- Others: Baby reportedly well; no acute findings documented about baby.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Suspected thromboembolism risk in the postpartum/post-cesarean patient with acute shortness of breath:
   - Assessment: Possible pulmonary embolism or other thromboembolic process (DVT/PE) considered.
   - Differential diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism; pneumonia/bronchitis; musculoskeletal chest pain related to deep breathing; postpartum-related pain.
   - Investigations planned: Urgent hospital evaluation recommended for further workup (imaging and clot assessment as indicated in hospital setting).
   - Treatment planned: If a clot is identified, treatment to reduce the clot (anticoagulation) may be given.
   - Referrals: Hospital admission or evaluation; patient advised to go to the hospital (either ambulance or self-transport with baby).
2. Medications/management considerations:
   - Advice to discontinue Codeine temporarily while being evaluated.
   - Avoid Ibuprofen due to known allergy.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No documented vitals (BP, HR by machine, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation), no physical exam details beyond patient-reported findings, no imaging or lab results available, no complete medication reconciliation beyond Codeine usage and Ibuprofen allergy.
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth provided inconsistently (patient stated April 20, 1980; physician noted 1983).
- Transcript quality: Conversation included gaps and informal statements; some details (exact vitals, full med list) were not captured in the chat. No major inaudible segments, but some phrasing was informal.
